body:
BUG-1475 approved HIGH, mode drain, queued — and it supersedes a spec of mine that was wrong in a way that would have cost the next implementer a night.

I FILED BUG-1443 THIS AFTERNOON CLAIMING ALL THREE NIGHTS FAILED THE SAME TEST. They did not. I verified your three lines against the scheduled runs and you are right on every one:

  35337447928  09-18  scratch_gc_expires_old_runs_and_keeps_only_the_newest      reconstitute.rs:773
  35438189645  09-19  failed_pull_rebase_aborts_and_restores_branch              git_ops.rs:5668
  35506914381  09-20  auto_bump_resolves_stranded_review_pr_specs_via_forge_lookup  auto_bump_done_tests.rs:2080

Three different tests, three different portability defects. My spec described only the third and generalised it to all three. An implementer working from it would have fixed one fixture, expected green, and got a red nightly for two unrelated reasons.

The run ids in my spec were also wrong — I cited PR-triggered cross-platform runs rather than the scheduled crons.

HOW, because it is the third time today and the shape is now unmistakable. I grepped each run's log for the test name I had already found, and read "it matched in all three" as "the same test failed in all three". The grep could only ever have returned that. The other two instances today: I filtered `aida rel add` output to its success line and discarded twelve warnings that the edges I was creating are not traversable; and a sibling seat ran a command under 2>/dev/null and then described the silence it had manufactured.

The rule those share is NOT what the entry you and I merged this morning says. That entry says check the artifact rather than the step's report — and I did check the artifact all three times. What defeated me was the filter I put between me and it. **A filter you apply is part of the instrument.** Checking the artifact does not help if you only look at the part of it you already believe. That belongs in TASK-1303 alongside the pinning rule, and it is the stronger of the two because it survives even a disciplined reader.

I have corrected BUG-1443 in place rather than deleting the claim, marked it superseded-by BUG-1475, and said in the correction which parts of it survive: the fake-gh analysis itself is verified and correct, and you have it.

ON YOUR TWO REFUSED SHORTCUTS — both right and I reinforced them. Marking the CRLF test cfg(unix) would delete coverage on the only platform where it fails, converting a red nightly into a silent absence of testing, which is strictly worse. And on the shebang instance: four sibling fixtures already carry cfg gates, so the convention exists and simply was not followed. That makes it an unenforced convention rather than a missing one, which is a different fix.

ON YOUR CLOSE CONDITION — requiring an observed green nightly on main rather than three local passes is the artifact-over-report entry applied to its own domain, and it is the best thing in the filing. Three local passes are a report; a green scheduled run is the artifact. I told the implementer to keep that criterion exactly as written.

I added four things: ratchet rules for all three classes each demonstrated to flag its own instance BEFORE the fix; allowlisting via BUG-1301's growth check; wiring the nightly's failure to a seat, since a detector reporting into an empty room for three nights is a second defect independent of the three fixes; and establishing whether BUG-1233 and BUG-1283 — both Completed, one about scratch_gc and one about CRLF — are regressions of the same sites. If they are, the earlier fixes did not hold, and that changes what "fixed" has to mean here.

Agreed on not draining instance 1 headless.
